subject: Reserved capacity proposal — scaling guardrails, discount thresholds, approval route
messages:
From: Jessica Lopez <jessica.lopez@bluesat.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@bluesat.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity interest — initial sizing and commercial guardrails

Hi Markus / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. BlueSat is evaluating a 24–36 month reserved capacity commit to service a new satellite imagery product (high throughput embedding + periodic batch generation at night). Before we put this in front of our procurement committee, we need a concrete proposal that includes:

- Suggested committed GPU sizing and a short rationale by workload (embedding vs. generation).
- Pricing tiers by commit size and term (12/24/36 months).
- Any proposed indexation or GPU-cost pass-through language (we have internal constraints around fixed vs. variable spend).
- Approval thresholds on Redwood side for discounts > X% and the expected internal timeline for approvals.

Can you send a concise proposal and the corresponding attachments (pricing spreadsheet + sensitivity model) by EOD Wednesday? Our committee meets next Friday.

Also loop legal — they will want the fallback capacity and outage SLA language up front.

Best,
Jessica Lopez
Head of Procurement — BlueSat Solutions
procurement@bluesat.com

Attachment: RFQ-BlueSat-20270607.pdf (reference only)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Lopez <jessica.lopez@bluesat.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity interest — initial sizing and commercial guardrails

Jessica — thanks for the clear ask and the RFQ. Attaching a short package: Redwood_reserved_pricing_v3.pdf and a GPU-cost-sensitivity-model.xlsx. High level summary below.

Summary (short):
- Recommended footprint: start with 40 reserved A100-equivalent GPU slots (mixed workload profile: 60% embedding throughput, 40% generation burst). Rationale: current request pattern + 2x nightly batch headroom.
- Term options & indicative net discount off list: 12mo (8%), 24mo (18%), 36mo (22%). Discounts shown assume flat GPU cost baseline.
- Cost-sensitivity: model shows that a 20% GPU market price increase would raise per-token costs ~12% with current batching assumptions; 20% reduction in GPU market price reduces cost ~13%.
- Proposed guardrails: indexation clause tied to public spot A100 price index with quarterly true-up capped at +/-7% per quarter and total annual band of +/-15%; optional collar (floor/ceiling) if BlueSat prefers fixed cap.

Approval & discounts: internal rule: any net discount >20% requires VP approval and finance sign-off; legal must review indexation language. For accelerated approval we can pre-authorize a one-off commercial exception for strategic deals, but that requires written sign-off from revenue ops + finance.

Next steps I recommend:
1) BlueSat picks term (12/24/36) and preferred indexation (fixed vs. true-up).
2) We run a final sizing sanity check with production telemetry (1–2 business days).
3) Redwood commercial ops issues a draft DocuSign MSA with the chosen pricing plan and the proposed fallback capacity.

I'm looping Ben for fleet planning comments and Laura for finance/approval lane.

- Markus
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_reserved_pricing_v3.pdf, gpu-cost-sensitivity-model.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Reserved capacity interest — initial sizing and commercial guardrails

Markus / Ben — quick internal note before we respond to BlueSat.

Thanks for the proposal, Markus. A few internal constraints we need to call out:
- Finance can approve up to 18% list discount for multi-year deals without escalation. Anything at or above 20% must go to the Revenue VP and require a finance risk memo.
- We need to avoid open-ended pass-throughs; legal will push for caps and explicit calculation methodology (index source + smoothing).
- For fleet planning: we should avoid a hard allocation that blocks capacity >60% for a single deal without recovery triggers (e.g., usage-based step-ups or release windows).

Suggested compromise to offer to BlueSat: 24-month term at 18% discount with a quarterly true-up tied to the A100 public index capped at +/-5% per quarter and a 10% annual band. Also include a "capacity safety" clause: if average utilization for the reserved pool is <50% for two consecutive quarters, Redwood may release up to 20% of the pool after a 60-day notice unless BlueSat opts into a committed ramp plan. This gives us a rollback mechanism.

Ben — can you confirm how that release window interacts with our current Dedicated fleet and whether we can honor scheduled burst capacity windows? Need a quick readout (1 day).

- Laura
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity interest — initial sizing and commercial guardrails

On Tue, Jun 8, 2027 at 09:35, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> Markus / Ben — quick internal note before we respond to BlueSat.
> 
> Suggested compromise to offer to BlueSat: 24-month term at 18% discount with a quarterly true-up...

Laura — quick fleet read: we can support a 40 GPU reserved pool with burst windows baked in (we'd route bursts to shared fleet with soft SLA for non-critical jobs). Releasing up to 20% after 60 days notice is operationally feasible but we should require a minimum 3-month capacity holdback during ramp to avoid churn.

On the sensitivity side, I ran an alternate scenario in gpu-cost-sensitivity-model.xlsx: if GPU spot index spikes 30% for two consecutive quarters, our marginal servicing cost goes up materially and we'd either need to: (a) invoke the quarterly true-up (if in contract), or (b) temporarily pause new batch jobs and honor latency SLAs for interactive traffic only. That scenario increases the risk of an SLA credit exposure; recommend we keep the +/-5% quarterly cap but allow a one-time emergency true-up with mutual approval if spot remains outside band for two quarters.

Recommendation: accept the 24-month @ 18% discount + quarterly true-up capped at +/-5% + 3-month ramp holdback + 60-day release notice for under-utilization. Finance to draft a short risk memo for deals that need any exception.

- Ben
Head, Dedicated Capacity Planning

Attachment referenced: gpu-cost-sensitivity-model.xlsx (see tab 'emergency-trueup')

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Lopez <jessica.lopez@bluesat.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@bluesat.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity interest — initial sizing and commercial guardrails

Jessica — thanks for patience while we vetted internally. Below is a concise proposal for BlueSat to review; I've included the attachments and a DocuSign link to a draft MSA for the 24-month path if you'd like to proceed quickly.

Proposal summary (one-pager):
- Committed footprint: 40 A100-equivalent GPUs (60% embedding, 40% generation).
- Term & commercial: 24 months at an 18% net discount off list.
- Indexation / true-up: Quarterly true-up tied to public A100 price index, capped at +/-5% per quarter and 10% annual band. Emergency clause: if index is outside the annual band for two consecutive quarters, parties agree to a one-time mutual true-up discussion (may include a temporary increase to pricing or temporary capacity prioritization).
- Capacity safety: Redwood may release up to 20% of reserved pool after a 60-day notice if utilization <50% for two consecutive quarters; a 3-month ramp holdback applies during initial onboarding.
- Approvals: This offer adheres to Redwood finance approval thresholds (no VP escalation required). Any deviation (discount >=20% or different indexation) will require VP revenue + finance sign-off and legal review.

If BlueSat is comfortable with the above, we'll:
1) run a 48-hr telemetry sanity check with your engineering team to validate the 40-GPU assumption.
2) issue a DocuSign draft MSA (attached link) for signature.
3) schedule a kickoff to align burst windows and monitoring hooks.

DocuSign draft: DOCUSIGN://envelopeId/0a1b2c3d
Drive package (pricing + sensitivity): https://drive.redwood.internal/DEAL-7834/commit-model

Please let me know if you'd like a variant: 12-month at 8% or 36-month at 22% (these would need explicit sign-off if you choose 36-month at the listed discount).

Best,
Markus Klein
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_reserved_pricing_v3.pdf, gpu-cost-sensitivity-model.xlsx, proposed-mop-docusign-link.txt
